en: The Ritual Manual for the Recitation of the One-Syllable Cakravartin King, translated according to the Sūtra spoken in the Tuṣita Heaven Palace:
I shall now proclaim this unsurpassed power, which excels all that is mundane and supramundane, the supreme among mantras.
The Ritual Procedure for the Recitation of the King of All Buddha-Uṣṇīṣas and the Uṣṇīṣa-Cakravartin: The practitioner should first purify themselves.
In a clean place, they should install an image of the Honored One (the deity).
Facing west, prostrate with the head to the ground;
receive the three refuges, relinquish the self, confess transgressions, and receive the precepts.
Having aroused the bodhicitta, rejoiced in merit, requested [the Buddhas to teach], made vows, and dedicated the merit, [proceed as follows].
One should bind the Samaya-mudrā of the Buddha Family:
interlace the four fingertips with one another,
and join the two wheels (thumbs) together, holding them upright.
The former is attached to the lid.
The heart-seal mantra of all Tathāgatas is as follows:
Oṃ īna-ni-ye (pronounced with the *ī* of *īna* and the *e* of *ni* joined). Second, perform the Lotus Samaya Seal.
This is the same mudrā as before;
however, the left wheel is bent and inserted into the palm,
while the right wheel is held upright as previously described.
This is called the Heart-Seal Mantra of the Lotus Family.
It is as follows: Oṃ aruli (1) vajrakulasamayamudrāṃ badhnīyāt (2).
This is the aforementioned Heart-Seal of the Lotus Family.
Bend the right wheel (finger) into the palm;
keep the left wheel upright as before.
This is called the Heart Mudrā of the Vajra Family. The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ vajra-tiṣṭha. Second, for the armor mudrā, follow the basic mudrā:
bend the two thumbs and rest them against the two index fingers.
One should seal the five locations—the back, the forehead, the right shoulder, the left shoulder, and the heart and throat.
The mantra is:
Oṃ cakravartini prasamita rādra rādra vāsamacaleśvari rakṣa rakṣa māṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. Next, one binds the Buddhalocanā mudrā.
Join the two hands in *añjali*.
Bend the two thumbs so that each rests against the back of its respective light-finger (*prabhā*).
Tuck the two index fingers into the palms.
The mantra for sealing the five places is:
Namo samantabuddhānām | Oṃ | Ruru saparu | Jvala tiṣṭha | Siddhalocane | Sarvārthasādhanī svāhā || Next, bind the Great Ocean Seal.
Interlace the two hands with the palms facing upward and spread the two wheels apart;
rotate them three times to the right while reciting the mantra of the Great Ocean: [Mantra follows]
Oṃ vimalanātha svāhā. Second, within the great ocean, one should visualize Mount Sumeru, composed of the four jewels.
Interlace the two hands inside, clench them tightly, and hold the fists upright; the mantra is:
Oṃ āñcara hūṃ. Second, visualize a jeweled pavilion atop Mount Sumeru.
Perform the seal of the Adhiṣṭhāna-ratnakūṭa.
The mantra for the Vajrapāṇi seal of both hands is as follows:
Namo samantabuddhānām | oṃ sarvathā khaṃ | uṃnāgite sphara hīṃ maḥ | oṃ oṃ na jñaṃ svāhā || Next, form the seal of the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa-cakravartin.
Interlace the palms with the fingers pointing inward to form fists.
Extend the two *raśmi* (rays) fingers, bending their upper joints like swords.
Extend both *cakra* (wheels) fingers together, bending the two *chhattra* (parasols) joints.
They support one another upon the two wheels.
The mantra for the protection of the five places is:
*Namo samantabuddhānāṃ* (1) *Varuṃ* (2). Next, perform the mudrā of the net-stake.
Following the previous root mudrā,
bend the upper joints of the two thumbs so that their backs do not touch.
Pressing with both wheels,
swing them up and down and rotate;
this constitutes the mantra for binding the upper and lower boundaries, which is as follows:
Namo samantabuddhānām. Aparājitaśasanānām. Oṃ vikiraṇa vicitrasani kapilavālini trāsaya vajravegasattvanotvara ṭvāṃ neṣṭara rakṣa svāhā. (8) Next, perform the mudrā of the wall.
Following the previous root mudrā,
bend the two joints of the two thumbs so they press against each other;
keep the two wheels (index fingers) level and upright, attaching them to the two thumbs.
Circumambulating three times to the right, it is thus accomplished.
The mantra for the Vajra Wall-Boundary (*vajraprākāra*) is as follows: *Namo* [as before]...
*Hūṃ* (1) *Mahoḥ* (2). Then, form the chariot-seal (*ratha-mudrā*).
Interlace the two hands with the palms facing upward and extend the two thumbs;
cause the sides of the nails to touch one another.
Bending the two wheels [feet] to rest beneath the base of the parasol,
visualize welcoming the Honored One from another world.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ tūru tūru hūṃ. Second, form the seal for welcoming the carriage.
This is modeled after the seal for the carriage:
with the two thumbs, point the tips of the light-fingers toward the head.
Wave three times toward one's own body.
The mantra is as follows:
*Vajrācārya-anujñāpayāmi namas-tīrthādhipataye tathāgatebhyaḥ oṃ vajragīte kṣaya svāhā*. Then, perform the mudrā for inviting [the deities].
Following the previous root mudrā,
bend the right hand behind the light and beckon three times toward the front.
The mantra is as follows:

*Namaḥ bhagavate apratihata-uṣṇīṣāya, ehy ehi svāgata dharmanarapratijñāne, argaṇa-danta-puṣpa-buddha-maline bhadre, mañca-vilokita, apratihatatejā-māraprakrama-maye svāhā.* Next, bind the seal of the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa for accomplishing all activities.
Interlace the two hands within;
extend the two index fingers upright like banners.
All offering substances, as well as the bathing water, cleansing earth, and so forth, [should be prepared].
Use this mantra for all purposes.
Whether for expelling obstacles, removing defilements, or establishing the boundary (sīmābandha), use this mantra.
For expelling, rotate it counter-clockwise; for establishing the boundary, rotate it clockwise. The mantra is as follows:
Namo samantabuddhānām. Oṃ taru-taru samaya svāhā. [Recite this] twice and re-form the previous net-stake mudrā (*jāla-kīla-mudrā*).
Bind the upper boundary.
Next, bind the seal of Aṣaṅgajihvā;
place the two hands side by side.
Cover the left with the right hand.
Firmly rotate the two wheels once to the right.
The mantra for forming the secret seam is as follows:
Oṃ āsaṃjñini hūṃ phaṭ. Second, form the offering *argha* mudrā;
it is based on the previous root mudrā, with the two thumbs bent and touching at their tips.
Attach two rays of light.
Vertically attach two wheels, each with a lid, to the sides of the root [mantra].
The mantra is as follows: Namo samantabuddhānām (1) oṃ (2) argaḥ (3) arga-pūjya (4) pratīccha hī-na-mañja-svāhā (5). Then, perform the fundamental mudrā twice.
Next, perform the mudrā for offering the lion throne.
It is based on the preceding root mudrā;
bend the two thumbs against the sides of the two wheel-nails.
The mantra is:
Oṃ ācaravīraya svāhā. Second, the mudrā for applying scented unguents (gandha):
it follows the previous root mudrā.
Bend the right prong downward and rest it against the lower joint of the right light. The mantra is:
*Namo samantabuddhānām | Oṃ trīlukye khanda-jāte hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā*. Fourth, perform the flower-offering mudrā.
Following the previous method for the *vilepana-mudrā* (incense-ointment seal),
change the left hand to cover [the right] and rest it upon the lower joint of the light on the right; the mantra is as follows:
Namo samantabuddhānām. Oṃ sarvalokapuṣṭipradāya hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā. Fourth, perform the incense-seal mudrā.
Following the previous root mudrā,
bend the two thumbs so that each rests against the lower joint of the ring finger. The mantra is as follows:
Namo samantabuddhānām. Oṃ vīrajetā-vijayā-dumaye hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā. (4) Next, perform the mudrā for offering food.
Following the previous root mudrā,
bend the upper joints of the two thumbs so that they each rest against the sides of the wheels. The mantra is as follows:
Namo samantabuddhānām. Oṃ sarvalokamaṇipriyāya hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā. Fourth, perform the mudrā for offering lamps.
Following the previous root mudrā, bend the two joints of the two thumbs so that they do not touch, and let each wheel rest upon its thumb. The mantra is:
Namo samantabuddhānām | Oṃ sarvalokasantrāsaśamanaye hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā. Fourth, perform the seal for the empowerment of universal offerings.
With both hands joined hollowly in *añjali*, the two joints of each of the five fingers are interlaced. The mantra is:
*Namaḥ sarvabuddhabodhisattvebhyaḥ | Oṃ sarvatathāgata-kuśumita-vijaya-rāśi-namaste svāhā*. Fourth, perform the seal of the All-Illuminating Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa (*Samantaprabha-buddhoṣṇīṣa-mudrā*).
Interlace the two hands within and form fists.
Cause the second joints of the index fingers (*tarjanī*) to slightly rise, and recite the mantra:
*Namo samantabuddhānām, oṃ mocana hūṃ*. Then, bind the seal of the White Parasol Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa (*Sitātapatrā-uṣṇīṣa*).
Twist each of the two wheels at the top of the two high *kavacas* so that their sides meet;
bend the two *kaṭaka*s into the shape of a lid.
The two light-rays curve slightly and join;
the two *śaktis* stand upright and join. The mantra is:
*Namaḥ samantabuddhānām, apratihataśāsānām, oṃ mama mā hūṃ ṇi svāhā*. Fourth, perform the seal of the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa of the gathered light.
Perform as before with the *Sitātapatrā* mudrā.
The mantra for opening the two canopies is as follows:

*Namo samantabuddhānām | apratihataśāsānām | oṃ tathāgatotsniṣa anavalokitamūrdhe jvaraśi hūṃ jvala jvala dhaka dhaka naramīnara cchinda bhinda hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā.* Next, bind the *Uṣṇīṣa* mudrā.
Following the previous *Sitātapatrā-mudrā*, bend the two thumbs to rest against the middle joints of the two index fingers. The mantra is:
*Namaḥ samantabuddhānām | apratihataśāsānām | oṃ jvala jvala bhīṣaṇe duṣṭanigraha huṃ phaṭ svāhā*. Fifth, form the *Uṣṇīṣavijayā-mudrā*.
Following the *Uṣṇīṣa-mudrā*,
move the two palms upward to the distance of two barley grains; the mantra is as follows:
Namo samantabuddhānām. Aparājitaśāsanānām. Oṃ jvalarajoyuṣṇiṣa hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. Next, perform the seal of the *Vijrīṇa* Buddha-uṣṇīṣa for subduing and destroying.
Interlace the two hands within to form fists;
extend the two "lights" (index fingers) and bend their upper joints,
with the right light pressing against the face of the left light.
To cause [the object] to emerge for about half a joint, the mantra is as follows:

*Namaḥ samantabuddhānām* (1) *apratihataśāsānām* (2) *oṃ* (3) *vikiraṇa* (4) *dhuna dhuna* (5) *duk* (6). Then, perform the *Buddhoṣṇīṣa-mudrā* (the Buddha-Crown Seal) to crush and destroy [the obstacles].
The same applies as before;
change "left light pillar" to "right light face," which also protrudes by about half a joint.
The mantra is as follows:
Namo samanta-buddhānām | Apratihata-śāsana-nām | Oṃ apratihatotsniṣāya sarva-vighna-vicchedana-kārāya trātāya svāhā. Next, bind the heart-seal of the Cakravartin-uṣṇīṣa.
Following the previous root mudrā, bend the two thumbs so they rest upon the upper joints of the two index fingers. The mantra for this is as follows:

Namo samantabuddhānām. Aparājitaśāsanānām. Oṃ tathāgataśroṣṇīṣāvalokito buddhanirghoṣavati hūṃ jvala jvala dhaka dhaka duna viduna trāsaya mārayūcara ya hana hana bhañja bhañja aṃ oṃ phaṭ kiṇi kuṇṭaliṇi aparājita-stara-dhariṇi hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. Next, form the heart mudrā.
Following the previous root mudrā, bend the two *kaṭaka* (fingers) and place them upon the upper joints of the two *raśmi* (fingers). The mantra is as follows:
*Namo samantabuddhānām | apratihataśāsānām | oṃ apratihatatejāya svāhā.* This is the Universal Buddha-uṣṇīṣa Mudrā.
With both hands hollowed and joined in the vajra-anjali gesture,
like a flower held within the palms;
if the practitioner is in haste and unable to bind all the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa mudrās in their entirety.
Simply bind this mudrā and recite the mantras of the various Buddha-uṣṇīṣas.
Next, bind the uṣṇīṣa-mudrā according to the previous root-mudrā.
Bend the right prong upward;
behind the right light, ensure they do not touch one another. The mantra is as follows:
Namo samantabuddhānām. Aparājitaśāsanānām. Oṃ cakravarmani oṃ hūṃ. (4) Next, perform the head mudrā.
Following the previous root mudrā, open the two lids and hold each upright behind the light rays so that they do not touch;
slightly bending them, the mantra is as before: "I take refuge... [and so forth].
Oṃ karmacakre hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. Then, again, bind the root mudrā.
Next, bind the Great Samaya Mudrā to provide protection for the deity.
Interlace the two hands with the palms facing inward.
Extend the two *raśmis* (rays) upward;
bend the two *cchatras* (umbrellas) behind the rays like hooks,
with a distance between them equal to that of a single grain of barley.
Place a lid upon each of the two wheels below the root [syllable].
Circumambulate three times clockwise while reciting the mantra:
Oṃ Śaṅkari Mahāsamaye Svāhā. Recite this one hundred and eight times as a hymn of praise.
If you wish to perform recitation,
first establish yourself as the principal deity through the five limbs,
or through the yoga of the five aspects of the principal deity.
Alternatively, one may visualize a single syllable at the crown, tongue, heart, and other locations.
This becomes the Principal Deity seated upon an eight-petaled lotus,
with seven jewels visualized upon each individual petal.
As before, one should visualize the Honored One Locanā upon a lotus petal.
Next, one should hold the rosary, according to what is taught in the Sūtra Spoken at the Site of Enlightenment (Bodhimaṇḍa).
Then, holding the rosary with palms joined.
Holding the rosary, recite the *Vimala-mani-dhāraṇī* seven times. The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ ānubodhi-vijaye siddhisiddhārthe svāhā. Third, perform the mudrā for holding the rosary.
With both hands, use the wheels to grasp the high armlets;
hold the two rays and the two banners upright,
and bend the two canopies behind the rays.
To ensure that [the hands] do not touch one another, the mantra for the half-vajra mudrā according to the Vairocana Sūtra is as follows:
Next, one should purify the mind; Recite the mantra according to the ritual while holding the rosary at the heart;
Fix the mind upon the tip of the nose.
The syllables and phrases are clearly articulated, neither too slow nor too hurried;
without frequent stretching, belching, or clearing the throat, one maintains a mind corresponding to the coughing and spitting of nasal mucus,
as well as a mind focused on painful sensations.
Such faults and afflictions as these shall all fail to arise when one is engaged in recitation; at that time,
body and mind must not become weary or indolent.
If you become weary, you should immediately form the mudrā of the five offerings,
recite praises, and present arghya water.
Upon completing the recitation, place the rosary upon the crown of your head.
Next, bind the previously mentioned seal of the secret seam;
by rotating it once counter-clockwise, the boundary is dissolved.
Next, bind the seal of respectful dismissal.
Following the previous root mudrā,
cover with the left hand and cast it outward while reciting the mantra for invitation.
Recite "chimi himi himi" and the phrase "kanyacha kanyacha";
this constitutes the ritual of respectful dismissal.
Next, one should again bind the mudrās of the wall, the net, the stakes, and so forth,
to protect the site above and below as well as the objects to be accomplished.
Next, bind the Kīlikīla mudrā.
Press the left wheel-mudrā upon the chest;
the tips of the remaining three fingers are spread apart and held upright,
forming the shape of a three-pronged vajra.
Having performed three clockwise circumambulations, the mantra for establishing the boundary (*sīmābandha*) is:
Oṃ kili kili vajra hūṃ phaṭ. Next, form the *Kumārī-mudrā*.
Second, cross the two hands at the palms;
bend the two [fingers] to press down high,
and use the two wheels to press down upon the high point.
Join the two light-fingers (tarjanīs) together.
Bend the two covering-fingers (aṅguṣṭhas) behind the light-fingers,
ensuring they do not touch by the distance of a single grain of barley.
After circumambulating three times to the right, the mantra for forming the boundary (*sīmābandha*) is as follows:
*Namo ratnatrayāya | namo vajrapāṇaye mahāyakṣasenāpataye | namo vajrakrodhāya | oṃ hulu hulu tiṣṭha tiṣṭha bandha bandha hana hana amṛte hūṃ phaṭ svāhā.* This is the single-syllable mantra.
As for fifteen characters,
calculate them by their number:
one *lakṣa* for each character.
Up to thirty syllables,
one should recite thirty lakṣas.
One should perform the preliminary rites.
If the text consists of thirty syllables or more,
one should recite it ten thousand times.
This is the *Recitation Ritual of the One-Syllable Cakravartin*.
